jobs.title: Director, Wealth Management Technology
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 258158

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Director, International Wealth Management is accountable for developing, leading, and overseeing delivery teams who are responsible for working with cross-functional development teams and business stakeholders to define and implement business strategies, product roadmaps, service offerings and new features.

The Director contributes to the long-term profitability of the International Wealth Management business line by establishing performance goals and work practices which drive the design and development of high-quality products and solutions.

This is a demanding hands-on and strategic role which requires the incumbent to be knowledgeable of the financial services sector and emerging trends in the Wealth and Asset Management industry.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

Management and oversight for delivery of a portfolio of initiatives focused on client and advisor solutions, ensuring that the deliverable align with strategic priorities.
Lead and drive a customer focused culture throughout the delivery teams to influence a client-centered design culture and to deepen relationships with business stakeholders and leverage broader bank relationships, systems, processes and knowledge.
Understand and keep up to date with emerging technologies, trends and innovative solutions across the industry.
Collaborate with business SMEs and technology teams to create platform roadmaps that align and assist in moving business strategies forward.
Provide guidance to stakeholders to ensure prioritization is driven by business value.
Define, lead and execute a cohesive strategy designed to limit technological debt and to effectively manage transition from legacy systems to modern technology platforms, maximizing operational efficiencies.
Excellent relationship building, influencing and negotiation skills to build and maintain strong supportive relationships with stakeholders across the organization.
Manage engagement with bank stakeholders and effectively communicate product release contents and expected product capabilities/customer journey.
Engage with the engineering and design teams to help determine the best technical implementation methods as well as a reasonable implementation schedule to launch products on a regular basis.
Manage communications and status reporting of ongoing initiatives, including summarizing project risks and options and facilitating prompt decisions when needed.
Maintain an understanding of financial services markets, the competitive landscape and digital transformation trends relative to the Wealth and Asset Management sector and client/user needs and requirements.
You possess a visionary and strategic leadership while inspiring team of solution architects and engineers to embrace your vision and be best in class team responsible for implementing and maintaining Wealth Technology solutions.
You are future focused with the ability to develop roadmaps and build business cases including benefits and costs
You thrive in providing strong leadership and driving employee empowerment and a high degree of engagement.
You excel in overseeing the architecture and design of solutions for the enterprise in a large and distributed environment.
You have experience delivering complex projects providing global, innovative solutions that improve the delivery of Wealth products
You excel in the assessment and selection of Global Wealth technologies and integration partners.
You excel in relationship, stakeholder management and influencing and negotiation skills, effective at all levels up to senior executives.
You can efficiently perform management tasks including incident response and escalations; vendor & contract management; infrastructure management and service resiliency; and service ownership.
You enjoy challenges of working on different types of projects (from large complex to simple).
You collaborate with various business functions to ensure Wealth Technology meets business needs.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

Individual projects range from Minor Enhancements ($50K+) to major strategic initiatives with $10MM+ budgets in a given year.
Demonstrated success delivering applications in an agile environment, strong organization and planning skills with a track record of successful delivery
Experience in leading and coaching delivery teams, with track record of attracting and developing talent
Critical thinking skills: using logic and reasoning to evaluate alternative solutions, recommendations, summarize conclusions and approaches to mitigate risks
Demonstrated ability to achieve strategic goals
Ability to develop strong working relationships with business and technology partners
Relevant working experience in the financial sector, Wealth and Asset Management experience
Understanding of the regulatory environment and parameters impacting the design and delivery of products and services within the Asset Management industry

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow & participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability & veterans.
Accessibility and Workplace Accommodations - We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank, and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.
Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days and benefits will start on day one.
Dynamic Ecosystem - Free tea & coffee, universal washrooms, and lots of space for team collaboration.
Community Engagement - We offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs such as hackathons.

Location(s): Canada : Ontario : Toronto

Scotiabank is a leading bank in the Americas. Guided by our purpose: "for every future", we help our customers, their families and their communities achieve success through a broad range of advice, products and services, including personal and commercial banking, wealth management and private banking, corporate and investment banking, and capital markets.

At Scotiabank, we value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank, and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Job Description:

***English job description follows***

Description de l'emploi :

Vous avez une expérience en transformation d’organisations de grande envergure, vous avez travaillé dans des programmes de transformation stratégique et/ou un environnement manufacturier et vous souhaitez évoluer et développer de nouvelles compétences? Ce poste est pour vous!

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un.e Responsable PMTD du développement industriel des nouveaux produits
(Procédés, Méthodes, Outils, Données) pour rejoindre notre équipe Performance et Amélioration opérationnelle basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous travaillerez conjointement avec les èquipes de la VSM, de transformation et de Toulouse en assurant la livraison end-to-end de toutes les versions PMTD industrielles pour atteindre la préparation des capacités VSM à travers toutes les fonctions.

Vous ferez partie de l’équipe excellence opérationnelle chargée de l'excellence et la performance opérationnelle.

L'organisation de l'équipe est établie de manière à promouvoir la collaboration transversale de manière autonome, en se soutenant mutuellement et en apprenant collectivement.

Votre rôle en tant que Responsable PMTD du développement industriel des nouveaux produits (Procédés, Méthodes, Outils, Données) sera de:

Concevoir la feuille de route PMTD;
Synchroniser la livraison entre toutes les parties prenantes;
Piloter la préparation et l'exécution des déploiements majeurs.

Votre environnement de travail:

Le siège du programme d'avions commerciaux A220 est situé à Mirabel, dans la région métropolitaine de Montréal, à deux pas de la ville dynamique de Montréal. Réputée pour son environnement paisible et sûr, la région offre une grande qualité de vie aux jeunes professionnels ou aux professionnels expérimentés, ainsi qu'aux familles, en équilibrant parfaitement les opportunités de carrière et les activités de plein air, ce qui en fait un endroit vraiment spécial où il fait bon vivre.

Parce que nous prenons soin de vous :

Avantages financiers: Salaire attractif, bonus annuel, régime d’assurances collectives, régime de retraite et régime d’achat d’actions.
Équilibre vie privée / professionnelle: Une politique de travail hybride (selon les besoins opérationnels), une cafétéria sur site, une politique de congés très concurrentielle.
Bien-être / santé: Programme d’Aide aux Employé.e.s (PAE), programme de rabais, service médical sur site, accès à un service de navette publique entre Laval (station de métro Montmorency) et Mirabel, et une application de covoiturage.
Développement individuel: Des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, mobilité nationale et internationale).

Vos défis:

Architecturer la feuille de route PMTD industrielle intégrée pluriannuelle en définissant la portée et la structure de toutes les versions;
Agir en tant que tour de contrôle PMTD industrielle, en synchronisant la livraison entre tous les flux et parties prenantes fonctionnelles (EU/CAN);
Piloter la préparation, la simulation et l'exécution des événements majeurs de transition ( Cutover ), en sécurisant la formation, la gestion du changement, la certification et la continuité opérationnelle post-déploiement;
Définir, exécuter et régir le transfert officiel des capacités à l'organisation opérationnelle ( Run - Fonctions Métiers & Digital) pour assurer la stabilité à long terme;
Assurer la livraison end-to-end de toutes les versions PMTD industrielles pour répondre aux défis du programme StepX;
Gérer l'exécution directe d'un budget de coûts non récurrents (NRC) de plus de 20 M$.

Votre profil:

Vous avez un baccalauréat / diplôme universitaire ;
Vous avez au moins 15 ans d'expérience pertinente ;
Vous détenez une certification en gestion de projet ( Project Management ) ;
Vous possédez un solide sens des affaires industrielles ( Broad Industrial acumen ) ;
Vous détenez une expérience avérée dans la direction de programmes de transformation stratégique et la traduction de la stratégie d'entreprise en livrables opérationnels ;
Vous avez la capacité à travailler avec une autonomie complète et à exercer une influence stratégique/transversale.

Ce travail nécessite une prise de conscience liée à tous les risques potentiels de conformité et à un engagement à agir avec intégrité, ces valeurs sont le fondement du succès, de la réputation et de la croissance durable de l'entreprise.

Vous ne semblez pas correspondre à 100%? Pas d'inquiétude! Airbus vous accompagnera pour trouver le poste qui correspond le mieux à vos compétences et aspirations.

Donnez une nouvelle dimension à votre carrière en soumettant votre candidature en ligne maintenant!

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
Company Description
Kraken Robotics is a global marine technology company focused on transforming subsea intelligence through advanced sensors, software, and integrated systems. The company serves defence, offshore energy, and ocean science markets by delivering actionable insights in demanding underwater environments. Its integrated subsea solutions span sonar, navigation, positioning, imaging, power, communications, monitoring, and data analytics. In 2026, Kraken Robotics acquired the Covelya Group, bringing together Sonardyne, EIVA, Forcys, Voyis, and Chelsea Technologies. This combined organization leverages highly skilled global teams and dual-use technologies to solve complex underwater challenges.

We are currently recruiting for a Director, Finance
to join our  Dartmouth, Nova Scotia Office.
This is a hybrid position, with an expectation of approximately three days per week on-site, with flexibility to work remotely on other days.

We are looking for an experienced finance leader to provide strategic and operational leadership for the Finance function within our Business Unit (BU).

This is a key leadership role for someone who enjoys being both a strategic business partner and a hands-on finance leader. You will work closely with the BU Managing Director and leadership team to support commercial decision-making, manage financial performance, and risk, and help drive sustainable business growth.

What You'll Do:

Financial Strategy & Business Partnership

Lead the development and execution of financial strategies that support BU priorities and long-term growth.
Act as a trusted financial adviser and business partner to the BU Managing Director and leadership team.
Provide financial modelling, scenario planning, and analysis to support strategic and commercial decisions.

Financial Management & Reporting

Oversee financial accounting, management reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning.
Maintain strong financial controls, systems, and policies in line with Group requirements and applicable regulations.
Take ownership of the BU's P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, and working capital performance.
Ensure monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting is accurate, timely, and meets stakeholder expectations.

Project & Commercial Finance

Partner with project and operational teams to support accurate project costing, budget management, and profitability.
Provide financial and commercial guidance on bids, tenders, capital expenditures, investments, and contract terms.
Monitor project margins and costs, identify variances, and recommend corrective actions where needed.

Compliance, Audit & Risk

Ensure compliance with applicable financial, statutory, tax, and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate BU audit activities and work closely with external auditors.
Identify financial risks and develop appropriate mitigation strategies.

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, coach, and develop the finance team, fostering a collaborative and accountable environment.
Support professional development and promote a high-performance culture.
Drive process efficiency and effective workload management across the team.

What We're Looking For

5+ years of experience in finance management or leadership roles.
ACA, ACCA, CIMA, or an equivalent professional accounting designation.
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field.
Strong commercial and business acumen, with experience partnering with financial and operational leaders.
Experience leading teams across multiple locations and working within a matrixed organization.
Experience in engineering, manufacturing, or project-based industries is highly desirable.

Skills That Will Help You Succeed

Strong knowledge of financial regulations, IFRS, and compliance requirements.
Excellent financial modelling, forecasting, and analytical skills.
Commercial mindset with the ability to translate financial information into meaningful business insights.
Strong proficiency in Excel and financial systems; experience with ERP or accounting software such as NetSuite is an asset.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and influencing skills.
Strategic thinker with strong attention to detail.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, project-driven environment.
Proactive, adaptable, dependable, and collaborative.

jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
ABOUT TRINDENT

Trindent Consulting is a global management consulting firm that specializes in technical augmentation in the energy sector, specifically downstream oil & gas and large energy users. We are a profit improvement firm, first and foremost. Trindent Consulting specializes in process engineering & optimization.
Without capital investment we create actionable ways to sustainably increase refinery margins by 2–3%. We’ve helped over 100 clients achieve significant financial benefits that yield between 500–1500% return-on-investment within the 1st year – and we’ve done that without capital investments or software changes of any kind.
Established in 2008, Trindent Consulting has quickly garnered a reputation as a firm that Makes It Happen™. We are ranked as one of Canada’s Fastest-Growing Companies by Canadian Business and GROWTH 500 for 7 years in a row. In September 2026 our 290% 3-Year Revenue Growth was rewarded with being named in Globe & Mail’s 2026 Fastest growing companies in Canada. Trindent Consulting is the 5th fastest growing Professional & Technical Services company in Canada.

Refineries are extraordinarily complex businesses. Trindent specializes in several ultra-high value niches within refineries where tens of millions of dollars in performance improvement may be captured in the short-term. Underpinned by data analytics, industry know-how, and technical experience; Trindent has implemented improvement engagements in over 40 refineries globally.

BUSINESS EXPANSION

Our practice is expanding. As part of this growth, we are building a strong pipeline of experienced professionals to support client engagements. We are gearing up for 20–25% growth and we hope you will join us on this journey!

THE OPPORTUNITY

Trindent Consulting is seeking a Director of Financial Planning & Analysis
to lead the evolution of Finance from a predominantly transactional accounting function into a commercially focused management finance organization.
This is a senior, hands-on leadership role responsible for building the planning, reporting, analytics and decision-support capabilities required to support Trindent’s continued growth. The Director will provide leadership with reliable financial information, actionable commercial insight and clear recommendations that strengthen operational control, improve project profitability, deliver measurable cost savings and enable better delegation of authority.
The successful candidate will establish an integrated view of Trindent’s financial and operational performance, connecting project revenue, consultant labour, utilization, expenses, margin realization, headcount, cash flow and investment decisions. They will work closely with the President, Finance Director, Executive and Leadership Teams, project leaders and functional budget owners to translate company strategy into financial targets, operating plans and accountable actions.

This role requires someone who can operate strategically while remaining close to the detail: building models, challenging assumptions, improving data quality, resolving reporting gaps and explaining financial performance clearly to senior leadership and the Board.

The Director of FP&A will be charged with establishing five foundational management finance capabilities.

1. Project-Based Financial Reporting

Design and implement a standardized Sold vs. Plan vs. Actual
reporting framework for all major assessments and engagements.
Provide clear project-level visibility into:
Contracted and recognized revenue.
Planned and actual consultant labour.
Consultant utilization and resource deployment.
Travel and other project expenses.
Gross margin and margin realization.
Forecast-to-complete and expected final project outcome.
Material financial and operational variance drivers.
Establish consistent project definitions, financial assumptions, data sources, ownership and reporting timelines.
Introduce recurring project financial reviews that identify emerging margin risks, delivery issues, corrective actions and accountable owners.
Ensure project reporting supports stronger engagement governance, resource planning, commercial decision-making and margin management.

2. Executive Management Reporting

Implement a reliable monthly management reporting package for the President, Finance Director, Executive and Leadership Teams.
Provide concise analysis of:
Revenue and project profitability.
Gross margin and operating performance.
Cash flow and working capital.
Budget and forecast variances.
Consultant utilization, headcount and labour cost.
Travel and operational expenditure.
Cost-saving performance.
Key risks, opportunities and required decisions.
Move reporting beyond retrospective results by explaining what happened, why it happened, what is expected next and what action is recommended
.
Clearly distinguish final, provisional, estimated and unavailable information, with named owners and deadlines for resolving material data issues.
Establish a recurring reporting calendar, review cadence and approval process that leadership can rely on.

3. Cost Savings and Expense Optimization

Launch a structured cost-optimization program covering travel, procurement, vendor management and operational spending.
Prioritize opportunities relating to:
Airline and hotel expenditure.
Foreign-exchange and payment fees.
Cancellation and change charges.
Vendor pricing and service levels.
Contract compliance.
Duplicate, avoidable or uncontrolled expenditure.
Quantify business cases, establish financial baselines and maintain a formal savings register.
Distinguish identified, approved, implemented and realized savings to ensure benefits are measurable and verifiable.
Turn cost analysis into practical recommendations on what to renegotiate, consolidate, defer, reduce or stop—without undermining client delivery or sustainable growth.

4. Governance and Financial Controls

Strengthen financial governance through clearer approval authorities, spending controls, vendor oversight, payment controls and project performance reviews.
Introduce vendor scorecards covering cost, service, responsiveness, contract compliance and performance.
Establish recurring financial and operating reviews with clear agendas, decision rights, actions, owners and completion dates.
Improve controls over budget commitments, purchase decisions, project expenditure and forecast changes.
Work closely with Accounting to define a disciplined month-end handover covering required inputs, reconciliation checks, delivery dates, data ownership and escalation routes.
Improve transparency and control while avoiding unnecessary bureaucracy or slowing operational decision-making.

5. Board and Leadership Readiness

Develop Board-ready financial reporting covering:
Overall financial performance.
Project and portfolio profitability.
Revenue, margin and cash-flow trends.
Operational and professional-services KPIs.
Material risks and opportunities.
Cost-optimization performance.
Progress against the Finance transformation roadmap.
Ensure Board and leadership materials are concise, accurate, reconciled and supported by clear analysis.
Maintain models, assumptions and supporting evidence in a due-diligence-ready state.
Provide the President, Finance Director and senior leadership with scenario analysis, recommendations and decision papers that enable confident and timely action.

QUALIFICATIONS

A recognized accounting or finance qualification such as CPA, CA, ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CFA or an equivalent professional designation.

KEY SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

10 years+ business and operational finance track record working for a fast growth services business operating across multiple legal entities, currencies & countries.
Experience in a consulting, professional-services, project-based or people-intensive business connecting project revenue, labour deployment, utilization, expenses, headcount and cash flow.
Experience building
or materially upgrading an FP&A function.
Advanced financial modelling, forecasting, scenario analysis and sensitivity analysis.
Strong project-profitability, margin-analysis variance, trend and root-cause analysis capability.
Strong data reconciliation, model-control and documentation discipline.
Advanced spreadsheet capability and experience working with ERP, planning, reporting or business-intelligence platforms.
Ability to design executive dashboards and communicate financial and operational KPIs clearly.
Strong business-case development, investment evaluation and decision-support capability.
Ability to translate complex financial information into concise, commercially relevant recommendations.

WORK LOCATION & FLEXIBILITY

This position may be based in either Dublin, Ireland or Toronto, Canada.

Trindent Consulting is looking for a FP&A Director who can modernize our financial reporting, provide deep insights and help us Make it Happen
as we grow our global revenues and customer base.

About GrandBridge Corporation

Who We Are:

GrandBridge Corporation is an investment holding company dedicated to driving growth and innovation through our fully owned subsidiaries, GrandBridge Energy Inc., and GrandBridge Group Inc.

GrandBridge Energy Inc. is a leading provider of innovative energy solutions, committed to delivering reliable and sustainable energy to our customers. GrandBridge Group Inc. offers a wide range of energy services through its divisions: Netoptiks, which provides cutting-edge telecommunications solutions, and Enersure, which ensures our customers' homes are comfortable and energy-efficient with home comfort rentals.

Our team of dedicated professionals are committed to helping our communities navigate the transition towards a dynamic and evolving energy landscape. The principles and beliefs that guide our operations are deeply rooted in our values. Join us in our mission to shape the future of energy.

Professional Development & Career Opportunities

About The Role:

As the Vice President, Finance & Chief Financial Officer (CFO), you will be a key member of the Executive Leadership team, reporting directly to the President & CEO. You will provide strategic leadership and executive oversight for finance, accounting, business and financial planning, treasury, tax, enterprise risk management, investor relations and procurement, while serving as a trusted advisor to the President & CEO, Board of Directors, and Executive Leadership team.

You will play a critical role in shaping the Corporation’s financial strategy, long-term sustainability, and overall business performance. As the Corporation’s senior financial executive, you will lead the development and execution of financial strategies that support growth across both regulated and competitive businesses, while ensuring sound governance, prudent risk management, disciplined capital allocation, and strong financial stewardship.

The Vice President, Finance & CFO will also play a significant role in evaluating mergers and acquisitions, strategic partnerships, and other significant investment opportunities, providing financial leadership and insight to support the Corporation’s growth strategy.

We are seeking an accomplished and forward-thinking leader with the strategic insight, financial acumen, and executive presence to help guide the Corporation through a period of continued growth and transformation. The successful candidate will be a collaborative and trusted partner who builds strong relationships, influences complex decisions, and leads with integrity, accountability, and a commitment to excellence. You will foster a high-performing, engaged team while advancing a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and exceptional service to customers, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

What You Will Do:

Strategic Leadership & Business Performance
:
Partner with the President & CEO, Corporate Development and Executive Leadership team to shape and execute our growth strategy across regulated and competitive businesses.
Provide strategic advice on enterprise strategy, capital deployment, growth, risk and financial implications of major decisions.
Lead financial strategies that support sustainable growth, operational excellence, and long-term value creation.
Align financial plans, resources, funding plans, and performance measures with corporate priorities.
Develop decision frameworks, scenarios, and performance insights that improve the quality and speed of Executive and Board decisions.
Champion accountability, innovation, continuous improvement, and data-driven decision-making.

Growth, M&A, and Competitive Business Development

Lead the financial evaluation of acquisitions, mergers, partnerships, joint ventures, new markets and business opportunities.
Develop transaction and financing structures that balance strategic value, financial returns, tax, regulatory requirements, and overall capital capacity.
Serve as a strategic partner by strengthening business models, pricing, investment governance, performance measures and scalable financial capabilities that support profitable growth.
Co-lead transaction integration and post-investment oversight, including financial systems, controls, cost allocation, synergy tracking and benefits realization, ensuring that approved investments deliver sustainable enterprise value.

Financial Stewardship and Transformation

Provide executive leadership for all finance, accounting and financial planning functions.
Ensure the integrity, accuracy and timeliness of consolidated and operating entity financial reporting, accounting, management information, and external disclosures.
Modernize finance systems, processes, data and analytics to improve efficiency, automation, forecasting accuracy, decision support and the scalability required for business growth and future acquisitions.
Maintain a strong system of internal control, delegated authority, financial policy and assurance that protects the company’s assets and reputation.
Lead enterprise budgeting, forecasting, and performance reporting, providing the President & CEO, Boards and Executive Leadership team with clear, forward-looking insights, and early identification of emerging risks and opportunities.
Support the Corporation’s ESG objectives through financial leadership, performance measurement, reporting, and decision support.

Treasury, Risk Management & Investor Relations:

Lead treasury, financing, liquidity, and capital structure strategies.
Manage effective relationships with municipal shareholders, lenders, rating agencies, and other key financial stakeholders.
Provide executive oversight of the Enterprise Risk Management framework.
Ensure that strategic, financial, transaction and emerging risks are identified, assessed and integrated into capital allocation, business planning, and executive decision making.
Oversee tax planning, compliance, and reporting activities.

Regulatory Affairs:

Advise the President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team and Boards on the financial, strategic and enterprise implications of regulatory policy, emerging requirements and industry developments, identifying opportunities, risks and recommended actions.
Translate regulatory decisions, commitments and emerging policy directions into the financial plans, capital strategy, forecasts, performance measures and risk-management priorities.
Provide executive-level financial leadership for major rate applications, capital funding mechanisms and regulatory initiatives, ensuring that revenue requirements, forecasts, cost allocation, and capital plans are credible, integrated and financially sustainable.
Lead engagement and advocacy with regulators, governments, sector organizations and other stakeholders to advance regulatory frameworks that enable innovation, investments, and improved outcomes for customers and communities.
Partner with General Counsel to integrate and align financial, legal, policy and regulatory perspectives in applications, advocacy, compliance and business development.

Procurement & Supply Chain:

Provide executive leadership and oversight for procurement and supply chain strategy.
Lead the transformation and integration of procurement and supply-chain capabilities, including processes, systems, data, analytics and supplier governance.
Establish procurement policies, controls, authorities, and performance measures and ensure procurement practices support value, transparency, compliance, and prudent risk management.
Promote strategic sourcing, supplier performance management, and continuous improvement.
Partner with business leaders to strengthen commercial decision-making and contract management.

What You Will Bring

Graduate degree in Commerce, Finance, Business, or related discipline, with a CPA designation.
Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in finance or accounting, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership or executive role.
Strong expertise in financial planning, accounting, treasury, capital management, enterprise risk management, and business performance.

Experience in the energy, utility, or other capital-intensive sector is preferred. Knowledge of the regulated business environment and regulatory processes is an asset.

SETUP
: Mostly remote, only required 1-2 times/month in office. Located in North York, ON

About the Opportunity

Financial Reporting & Consolidations:
Lead the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual consolidated financial statements and management reporting.
Oversee the consolidation of multiple legal entities/business units, including intercompany balances, eliminations, foreign currency translation, and consolidation adjustments.
Ensure financial reporting is accurate, complete, appropriately supported, and delivered within established reporting timelines.
Maintain and enhance consolidation processes, reporting packages, and financial controls.
Partner with business units and finance teams to resolve consolidation and reporting issues.

US GAAP & IFRS:
Serve as a key technical accounting resource for matters involving US GAAP and IFRS.
Research and assess complex accounting issues and provide recommendations regarding appropriate accounting treatment.
Monitor new and emerging accounting standards and assess their impact on the organization.
Lead the implementation of new accounting standards and changes to existing reporting requirements.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos, position papers, and supporting documentation.
Support accounting matters involving areas such as revenue recognition, leases, business combinations, foreign currency, impairment, and other complex transactions, as applicable.

Controls, Audit & Compliance:
Maintain a strong financial control environment across the reporting and consolidation processes.
Coordinate with internal and external auditors and support quarterly and annual audit requirements.
Ensure appropriate documentation and supporting schedules are maintained for significant accounting judgments, estimates, and transactions.
Identify reporting and control risks and implement process improvements to strengthen financial governance.
Leadership & Business Partnership:
Lead, coach, and develop a team of 4–5 finance and accounting professionals, establishing clear responsibilities and development priorities.
Provide technical guidance and oversight to the team while promoting accountability and high-quality execution.
Partner closely with FP&A, Corporate Accounting, Tax, Treasury, and other finance functions to ensure consistency and accuracy across financial reporting.
Work with senior leadership to communicate financial reporting matters, accounting implications, and significant issues.
Support acquisitions, integrations, restructuring activities, and other strategic initiatives from an accounting and reporting perspective.

Process Improvement:
Drive improvements to the financial close, consolidation, and reporting processes with a focus on accuracy, efficiency, standardization, and scalability.
Identify opportunities to automate manual reporting and reconciliation activities.
Strengthen reporting processes, systems, and controls as the organization grows and reporting requirements evolve.

About You

CPA designation.
10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including significant experience in a leadership capacity.
Strong technical knowledge and practical application of US GAAP and/or IFRS.
Significant experience with multi-entity consolidations, including intercompany eliminations and foreign currency considerations.
Experience leading and developing accounting or financial reporting teams.

Description de l'emploi :

Vous avez une expérience en transformation d’organisations de grande envergure, vous avez travaillé dans des programmes de transformation stratégique et/ou un environnement manufacturier et vous souhaitez évoluer et développer de nouvelles compétences? Ce poste est pour vous!

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un.e Responsable PMTD du développement industriel des nouveaux produits
(Procédés, Méthodes, Outils, Données) pour rejoindre notre équipe Performance et Amélioration opérationnelle basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous travaillerez conjointement avec les èquipes de la VSM, de transformation et de Toulouse en assurant la livraison end-to-end de toutes les versions PMTD industrielles pour atteindre la préparation des capacités VSM à travers toutes les fonctions.

Développement individuel: Des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, mobilité nationale et internationale).

Vos défis:

Architecturer la feuille de route PMTD industrielle intégrée pluriannuelle en définissant la portée et la structure de toutes les versions;
Agir en tant que tour de contrôle PMTD industrielle, en synchronisant la livraison entre tous les flux et parties prenantes fonctionnelles (EU/CAN);
Piloter la préparation, la simulation et l'exécution des événements majeurs de transition ( Cutover ), en sécurisant la formation, la gestion du changement, la certification et la continuité opérationnelle post-déploiement;
Définir, exécuter et régir le transfert officiel des capacités à l'organisation opérationnelle ( Run - Fonctions Métiers & Digital) pour assurer la stabilité à long terme;
Assurer la livraison end-to-end de toutes les versions PMTD industrielles pour répondre aux défis du programme StepX;
Gérer l'exécution directe d'un budget de coûts non récurrents (NRC) de plus de 20 M$.

Votre profil:

Vous avez un baccalauréat / diplôme universitaire ;
Vous avez au moins 15 ans d'expérience pertinente ;
Vous détenez une certification en gestion de projet ( Project Management ) ;
Vous possédez un solide sens des affaires industrielles ( Broad Industrial acumen ) ;
Vous détenez une expérience avérée dans la direction de programmes de transformation stratégique et la traduction de la stratégie d'entreprise en livrables opérationnels ;
Vous avez la capacité à travailler avec une autonomie complète et à exercer une influence stratégique/transversale.

Ce travail nécessite une prise de conscience liée à tous les risques potentiels de conformité et à un engagement à agir avec intégrité, ces valeurs sont le fondement du succès, de la réputation et de la croissance durable de l'entreprise.

Donnez une nouvelle dimension à votre carrière en soumettant votre candidature en ligne maintenant!
